Jordan / Team — see summarized legal position below. I'm attaching a short redline summary and a vendor attestation template you can circulate to the subprocessors. Key flow-downs we require in the annex and associated order form language: 

- Data handling: subprocessors must be bound to identical data processing obligations (purpose limitation, deletion/return obligations, encryption-in-transit/at-rest).
- Subprocessor approvals: Redwood to maintain an approved subprocessor list; material changes trigger notice to Brightline within 30 days and allow Brightline to object and request mitigation or alternative controls.
- Audit & evidence: subprocessors supporting production data must provide SOC2 Type II or equivalent; if not available, a signed attestation and a security questionnaire are required.
- Cascade termination: if a subprocessor's control failure materially impacts Brightline, Brightline may require removal or termination of that subprocessor as a condition to continue the Order Form.
- Liability carveouts: maintain mutual limitations but ensure indemnities for gross negligence/breach of security obligations.

Please review the attached redline_summary.txt (high level) and the vendor_attestation_template.pdf. If Brightline wants a DocuSign-ready annex, we can produce one once we settle redlines.

Attachments: redline_summary.txt; vendor_attestation_template.pdf

— Jonas Weber
